Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

netify 1.5.4

Behavior changes

These fixes change numbers that earlier versions reported.

  • summary() density excludes dyads with missing values from the denominator, matching sna::gden(). Networks without missing dyads are unaffected.
  • Matrix, array, and list inputs whose diagonal is entirely zero are now read as having no self-loops (diag_to_NA = TRUE), matching the igraph import path. Pass diag_to_NA = FALSE to keep self-loop cells in density and summary_actor() prop_ties.
  • to_netify() sets the diagonal of imported statnet network objects that do not allow loops to NA, matching the igraph import. Density for these networks now agrees with sna::gden(), and netify to statnet to netify round trips keep their density.
  • netify(..., output_format = "longit_array") respects actor_pds and actor_time_uniform = FALSE. Actors outside their active periods are NA in those periods.
  • Supplying actor_pds with gapped numeric time no longer creates empty periods for every integer in the range.
  • The stored actor_pds (and get_actor_time_info(net)) uses time labels in the class of the time variable rather than integer positions.
  • mixing_matrix() counts each undirected tie once, so total_ties is halved for symmetric networks and raw between-group cells hold half a tie in each mirrored cell. Proportions, assortativity, and modularity are unchanged.
  • compare_networks() counts each undirected edge once in edge_changes. For networks with different actors, correlation, Jaccard, Hamming, QAP, and spectral distance are computed on the shared actors, with a message saying how many actors were left out.
  • bootstrap_netlet() resamples longitudinal netlets by actor name, so the same actors are drawn in every period. Pairs formed by two copies of the same actor are NA rather than 0, removing a downward bias in density.
  • subset(from =, to =) on unipartite networks returns a square matrix over the union of the selected actors, with ties outside the from x to block set to NA.

New warnings and messages

  • netify() warns when symmetric = TRUE and a dyad appears in both directions within a period with different weights. The value from the last row is still used; use sum_dyads = TRUE, aggregate_dyad(..., symmetric = TRUE), or symmetric = FALSE to resolve it.
  • nodal_vars is documented as describing actor1, and netify() reports actors that only appear as actor2, since they receive NA.

Bug fixes

Subsetting and transformations

  • subset() / subset_netify() on longitudinal networks clips actor period bounds to the retained periods. Subsetting to several periods without both endpoints previously made plot(x, time_filter = ...), decompose_netify(), and add_node_vars() fail with “Actor period bounds are not in the netlet time labels.”
  • subset() returns requested periods in netlet order without duplicates.
  • subset() down to a single period keys dyadic data as cross-sectional, so dyad_correlation(), attribute_report(), add_dyad_vars(), mutate_weights(), and pivot_dyad_to_network() find existing dyadic variables.
  • subset() of a multilayer longitudinal array to one period returns a cross-sectional [actor, actor, layer] array.
  • subset() on a bipartite network gives a clear error when the selected actors come from only one mode.
  • ego_netify() subsets actor_pds, nodal, and dyadic attributes to the ego network’s actors and periods, and keeps the period name when only one period remains.
  • mutate_weights() with only add_constant changes longitudinal arrays, updates weight attributes on every period of a longitudinal list, renames the layer of single-layer networks with new_name, and works on multilayer networks. binarize() also works on multilayer networks.

Construction and attributes

  • nodal_vars, dyad_vars, add_node_vars(), and add_dyad_vars() work with POSIXct time.

Plotting

  • plot() draws each tie once in undirected networks.
  • plot() works for bipartite networks where an actor appears in both modes (for example mexico). summary_actor() returns plain actor names for these networks with an actor_mode column.
  • plot(..., static_actor_positions = TRUE) works for longitudinal bipartite networks.
  • layout = "sugiyama" works in plot() and get_node_layout().
  • point_layout accepts a single data.frame reused across periods.
  • plot_homophily(type = "distribution") works for longitudinal networks.
  • label_size_by, label_color_by, label_fill_by, and label_alpha_by no longer trigger an “Unknown parameter” warning.
  • node_filter in longitudinal plots removes edges only in the periods where an endpoint is filtered out.
  • time_filter accepts numeric time labels such as time_filter = 2012 when they are not valid indices, and lists the available periods when nothing matches.

Analysis

  • homophily(), mixing_matrix(), attribute_report(), and dyad_correlation() work on multilayer longitudinal netlets stored as lists.
  • homophily(method = "hamming") and method = "jaccard" accept character, factor, and logical attributes.
  • dyad_correlation() aligns dyadic covariates to network actors by name.
  • compare_networks(by = ...) works for what = "structure", "nodes", and "attributes", and gives a clear error for edge comparisons.

Converters

  • netify_to_statnet() accepts factor and Date nodal attributes.
  • netify_to_amen(lame = TRUE) and to_lame(lame = TRUE) order Xrow and Xcol rows to match each period’s actors.
  • The to_lame()$ame_call snippet runs with current lame, and from_lame_fit() returns a longitudinal netify for longitudinal lame::lame() fits.

Documentation

  • The animate_netify() example runs only when gganimate is installed.
  • The peek() example uses actor names that exist in icews.

netify 1.5.3

CRAN release: 2026-06-30

  • CRAN resubmission: shorten plot.netify(), compare_networks(), and netify_to_statnet() examples so they run quickly on CRAN Windows checks.

netify 1.5.2

  • CRAN resubmission: remove the obsolete C++11 standard request and update DESCRIPTION wording flagged by CRAN incoming checks.

netify 1.5.1

  • Fixed unnetify() and plot() for bipartite networks so ties in same-position row and column entries are kept. These entries are valid cross-mode ties, not diagonal self-ties.

netify 1.5

  • New worked example dataset (classroom_edges, classroom_nodes) and a matching short-form vignette (quickstart_inference) for quick onboarding.
  • Index of common pipelines available at ?netify_workflows, covering unipartite, bipartite, longitudinal, and multilayer setups, plus handoff to statnet, amen, lame, dbn, and igraph.
  • to_lame() now bundles posterior round-tripping via from_lame_fit(), including bootstrap and per-cell credible-interval bounds for binary bipartite fits.
  • bind_netifies() gains align_actors = c("none", "union", "intersection") for combining cross-sections with mismatched actor sets.
  • New helpers: drop_na_actors(), binarize(), validate_netify(), bootstrap_netlet(), compare_to_null(), simulate.netify(), plus type predicates (is_binary(), is_bipartite(), is_longitudinal(), is_multilayer(), n_actors(), n_periods(), n_layers()) and accessors (nodal_data()).
  • tidyverse and broom interop: as_tibble.netify(), tidy.netify(), glance.netify(), plus as.igraph.netify() and as.network.netify() S3 methods registered automatically when the relevant package is attached.
  • Plotting picks up style = "heatmap" for adjacency-matrix views, auto-diverging palettes for signed weights, smarter label-repel for small networks, and two extra themes (theme_publication_netify(), theme_publication_netify_ts()).
  • summary_actor() gains a stats = "fast" mode (skips the expensive centralities) and auto-promotes for networks above getOption("netify.fast_threshold", 1500).
  • Vignettes expanded and reorganized: pipeline_netify_ergm, pipeline_lame_dbn, multilayer_networks, tracking_changes, attribute_analysis, manual_plotting, and internals are all new or substantially rewritten.
